summary:

thesis: This episode argues that a small number of mega-cap technology companies, specifically Amazon, Meta, Netflix, Google, and Microsoft, were the primary drivers of the S&P 500's returns over the last decade. It contrasts this concentration with other major entities like Intel, Berkshire Hathaway, General Motors, and Intuit, which were not considered key winners during that same period.

claims.claim: Amazon is one of the few companies that has driven the majority of returns in the S&P 500 over the last decade.
claims.quote: Like in the last 10 years, it's been Amazon, Apple, Google, Microsoft, Facebook, Netflix. That's everything. And if you are a stock picker and you did not own those companies, if you just didn't own those and you put in all your effort to finding what are the other great companies outside of Fang, the odds that you've outperformed over the last decade, it's not zero, but it's they're very low.
